answers.ask: How long should a lane be - a compact map you see at a glance, or a sprawling route?
answers.answer: Use a compact lane that players can largely see at a glance, keeping each map optimized and easy to play across PC, mobile, and console.

answers.ask: Should all five maps share one lane layout with different dressing, or should each have its own route?
answers.answer: Each of the five maps should have its own distinct enemy route, matching its different setting and environmental obstacles.

scene_prompt: Create a realistic, modern 3D Tower Defense experience with a detailed central lobby: a main waiting plaza with several match-entry elevators arranged around it. Build exactly five compact battle maps, each designed so players can see most of its enemy lane at a glance, with a clearly marked enemy entry point, a defended base endpoint, designated tower-placement ground beside the lane, and blocked or unsuitable placement areas along paths and obstacles. Give every map a distinct route and environmental layout: a modern city with streets weaving between urban structures; a forest with a trail around trees and natural obstacles; a desert with a route through dunes and rock formations; an industrial area with lanes between factories, pipes, and machinery; and a military zone with a defended route through fortified structures and barriers. Use detailed models, quality textures, clear lighting, environmental cover, and readable combat space without obstructing visibility.
agent_notes: Self-declared 3D Tower Defense, so Strategy leads, and the bosses, targeting, upgrades and difficulty voting are systems on top of one defended route rather than a second layout genre. Shape is lane-actor-track: every map is specified as a clearly defined path from an enemy entry point to a goal with valid and invalid tower ground either side, and the answer gives each of the five maps its own distinct route — that continuity requirement is the P6 and it is not overridable. P4 follows from the five separate maps plus the lobby the elevators teleport out of, which cannot share one surface. Decided without a user: cover-los carries the per-map obstacles and environmental elements the prompt asks for, the tower preview and range circles are UI rather than layout so they are dropped from the handoff, and the compact see-it-at-a-glance lane from the answer sets the scale for all five maps.
